dimensions.assessment: Affects communities planning ecosystem restoration projects in designated floodways, professional engineers, and FEMA administrators.
dimensions.evidence: an ecosystem restoration project within an adopted regulatory floodway that would result in an increase in base flood elevations

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative and fee exemptions for specific local projects while restricting changes to situations where no insurable structures or critical infrastructure are adversely impacted.
dimensions.evidence: a requester shall be exempt from submitting a review or processing fee for a request for a flood insurance rate map change

dimensions.assessment: Removes review and processing fees for certain map change requests related to ecosystem restoration projects.
dimensions.evidence: a requester shall be exempt from submitting a review or processing fee for a request for a flood insurance rate map change

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeowner Flood Insurance Affordability Act of 2014 to add new conditions under which communities may permit certain floodway projects.
dimensions.evidence: Section 22 of the Homeowner Flood Insurance Affordability Act of 2014 (42 U.S.C. 4101e) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change affecting local floodway management and FEMA guidance issuance.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act... the Administrator shall issue guidance

missing_information: Exact number of communities or projects expected to utilize this exemption.
Dollar amount of waived review and processing fees.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes specific conditions and fee exemptions for ecosystem restoration projects in designated floodways that increase base flood elevations, affecting local communities, project requesters, and FEMA.
